articles.expand: USDCAD is pushing to its highest level since April 2025 as broad US dollar buying and higher Treasury yields give the pair another lift. A tightening Swiss central bank alongside a hiking Fed changes the usual rate-differential story for the franc. Combined with strong safe-haven demand during the equity rout, that could keep the franc well bid, especially against the euro. That is the very currency risk Martin flagged, so the SNB may stay willing to lean against excessive franc strength even as it tightens. articles.expand: A drop this deep, alongside the first easing in input cost inflation for months, weakens the case for further Australian monetary tightening. That leaves the Australian dollar exposed if rate markets start pricing a gentler path. The sharp fall in new export orders also points to softening external demand, at a time when global equities are already under heavy pressure. Prices are still running above their long-run averages, though, so policymakers are unlikely to move quickly to declare inflation beaten. articles.title: A December BoJ hike may not be enough: why a fuzzy endpoint keeps yen bears circling
articles.expand: With a December hike largely priced, the yen’s direction now hinges on the BoJ’s guidance beyond it. A vague statement or a cautious press conference from Ueda on December 18 risks a “hike and sell” reaction like last December’s. A clearer commitment to keep tightening toward 2% would give the yen more durable support. Until then, intervention risk near 160 is doing more to cap USD/JPY than rate expectations are. The July board changes add a longer-dated dovish tail risk that could weigh on yen forwards. --- The BoJ is agreed on December but divided on the destination, and that missing endpoin...

articles.title: Some analysts now see BoJ rates at 2.5% by mid-2027, despite slower underlying inflation
articles.expand: A 2.5% BoJ path is far from priced, so the forecast is more a marker of upside risk than a market mover. If the coming months show underlying inflation turning higher, front-end JGB yields would be the first to reprice, with the yen likely to follow. The view also raises the stakes for the BoJ’s December 18 statement and Ueda’s press conference, where any hint of a faster pace would carry weight. With energy and imported costs feeding producer prices, oil and USD/JPY remain the key inputs to watch. --- October’s slower underlying inflation hasn’t deterred the BoJ hawks: some forecasters now se...

articles.title: Japan CPI misses on all three measures, but core stays above 2% ahead of a BoJ hike call
articles.expand: The misses take a little edge off December hike pricing, but not enough to change the base case after Ueda’s hawkish remarks on Thursday. A slower underlying gauge leaves the yen with less support than it needed near 160, so the burden falls on intervention warnings rather than rate expectations. JGB yields may ease at the front end, but producer prices running at 7.1% keep the inflation pipeline full.
